land.text: the Tongan islands: Tongatapu, ʻEua, Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas

successors.note: Not a direct handover: 'In 1799, the 14th Tu'i Kanokupolu, Tuku'aho was murdered, which sent Tonga into a civil war for fifty years'; Tāufaʻāhau's kingdom unites the islands in 1845. The land is nobody's (warring chiefdoms of Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and Tongatapu) in 1799-1844.

capitals.note: Lapaha page: Muʻa was 'later (twelfth to sixteenth century CE) the capital of the Tuʻi Tonga Empire', 'famous for the ancient langi (royal burial tombs)'; the Tuʻi Tonga page has 'the Tu'i Tongas had their throne moved by the lagoon at Lapaha, Tongatapu'. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: Tongatapu, the island of ʻAhoʻeitu's line

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: the Tuʻi Tonga line's home island, before the 12th-century extent. '950 CE: ʻAhoʻeitu' is the infobox start. Soft: the page gives no boundary for the early realm.

correction.text: the Tongan islands: Tongatapu, ʻEua, Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the whole Tongan group as direct territory from the 12th century ('By the 12th century, Tongans, and the Tongan kings named the Tu'i Tonga, were known across the Pacific'; 'the empire had already stretched from Tikopia in the west to Niue in the east'). The tributaries (Samoa, ʻUvea and Futuna, Lau, Niue, Rotuma, Tokelau) are vassal tints in the ledger, not part of this shape. No area figure exists to compare; the page's peak is 'during the period 1200-1500'.

region.text: Tongatapu, the island of ʻAhoʻeitu's line

ledger.note: 950: ʻAhoʻeitu, first Tuʻi Tonga, begins to expand his rule beyond Tonga. Infobox '950 CE: ʻAhoʻeitu'; History of Tonga: 'In 950 AD Tu'i Tonga 'Aho'eitu started to expand his rule outside of Tonga.' The page also has 'ʻAhoʻeitu brought his faction to Samoa: 950'. The core is Tongatapu; the page gives no boundary.

region.text: the Tongan islands: Tongatapu, ʻEua, Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas

ledger.note: 1100: the Tongan group under the Tuʻi Tonga. Bridging event: 'By the 12th century, Tongans, and the Tongan kings named the Tu'i Tonga, were known across the Pacific' and 'the empire had already stretched from Tikopia in the west to Niue in the east'; the page does not date the incorporation of Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas, which is placed at the century's start.

region.text: Samoa except the Manuʻa group, which 'stayed under Tui Manuʻa rule'

ledger.note: 1100: Samoa pays tribute to the Tuʻi Tonga. 'By the time of Momo and Tuʻitātui, it included much of the former domains of the Tui Fiti and Tui Manuʻa. The Manuʻa group was the exception and stayed under Tui Manuʻa rule'; tribute (ʻInasi) was 'paid annually at Muʻa by tributary chiefdoms'. The year is this dossier's placing of the undated Momo-Tuʻitātui period (10th-11th Tuʻi Tonga).

1100: the eastern Fijian islands within the Tongan realm. 'Their realm contained Wallis and Futuna, Tokelau, Tuvalu, Rotuma, Nauru,' and continues with 'parts of Fiji, Kiribati, Niue, and Samoa'. The page gives no year; the 12th-century extent is used.

1100: Niue, Rotuma and Tokelau as tributaries. Same sentence as above ('Their realm contained Wallis and Futuna, Tokelau, Tuvalu, Rotuma, Nauru ... Niue'); the Tuʻi Tonga page cites Niue and Rotuma only for 'Tongan cultural influence'. Nauru, Kiribati and Tuvalu are not drawn: the Tuʻi Tonga page says Niutao in Tuvalu repelled Tongan invasions in the 15th and late 16th centuries.

region.text: Samoa except the Manuʻa group, which 'stayed under Tui Manuʻa rule'

ledger.note: 1250: Samoa expels the Tongans. 'In the 13th or 14th century Samoa defeated Tu'i Tonga Talakaifaiki under the lead of the' brothers Tuna, Fata and Savea, ancestors of the Malietoa; 'The Samoans then expelled the Tongans' (Tuʻi Tonga page). The year is the midpoint of the page's two centuries.

1450: Tongan invasions bring ʻUvea and Futuna under the Tuʻi Tonga. 'Tongan invasions in the 15th and 16th centuries. Futuna kept more of its earlier culture, while Uvea changed more.' The History of Tonga page lists Wallis and Futuna in the realm; the year is this dossier's placing of 'the 15th century'.

1535: the Haʻa Takalaua line takes effective rule. 'Takalaua was assassinated, and his successor Kauʻulufonua I founded the Haʻa Takalaua dynasty', his brother Moʻungamotuʻa holding the new Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua office; 'The Tuʻi Tonga decline began due to numerous wars and internal pressure.' Same state, same colour: the sacred Tuʻi Tonga remains, the secular line governs.

1535: the outer tributaries fall away with the Tuʻi Tonga's decline. Bridging event dated to Takalaua's assassination: 'The Tuʻi Tonga decline began due to numerous wars and internal pressure'; the page gives no year for the end of tribute from Fiji.
1535: tribute from Niue, Rotuma and Tokelau lapses. Same bridging judgment as the Lau event; the page gives no year.

1600: the Tongan hold on ʻUvea and Futuna ends with the 16th-century invasions. The page says only 'Tongan invasions in the 15th and 16th centuries'; the end of the 16th century is this dossier's placing.

1610: the Tuʻi Kanokupolu line is created. 'In 1610, the 6th Tuʻi Haʻa Takalaua, Moʻungatonga, created the position of' Tuʻi Kanokupolu for his half-Samoan son Ngata (History of Tonga: 'created the position of Tu'i Kanokupolu for his half-Samoan son, Ngata'). Same state, same colour.

region.text: the Tongan islands: Tongatapu, ʻEua, Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas

ledger.note: 1799: the murder of Tukuʻaho breaks Tonga into warring chiefdoms. 'In 1799, the 14th Tu'i Kanokupolu, Tuku'aho was murdered, which sent Tonga into a civil war for fifty years.' The Tuʻi Tonga title itself survives to Laufilitonga (1827-1865) and is abolished in 1865 (Tuʻi Tonga page infobox); Tāufaʻāhau's Kingdom of Tonga reunites the islands in 1845 (kingdom-of-tonga).

wars.name: Samoan expulsion of the Tongans

zones.text: Samoa except the Manuʻa group, which 'stayed under Tui Manuʻa rule'

wars.outcome: Tuʻi Tonga Talakaifaiki defeated by Tuna, Fata and Savea; the Tongans expelled from Samoa and the Malietoa title founded.
wars.note: Dated by the page only to 'the 13th or 14th century'; 1250 is the midpoint. Drawn as the vassal_end, not as a contest, since the page gives no campaign years.

wars.name: Tongan civil war (from 1799)
belligerents: Haʻapai and Vavaʻu chiefs (Tāufaʻāhau, Finau ʻUlukālala)

zones.text: the Tongan islands: Tongatapu, ʻEua, Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas

wars.outcome: Fifty years of civil war after Tukuʻaho's murder in 1799; Tāufaʻāhau of Haʻapai (1820) takes Vavaʻu (1833) and Tongatapu (1845) and founds the Kingdom of Tonga.
wars.note: 'sent Tonga into a civil war for fifty years'; 'the islands were united into a Polynesian kingdom in 1845'. The war lies after this state's end; it is listed so the reviewer sees the interregnum was considered. Reviewer (oc-01): 'to' clipped from 1845 to 1799, this state's end (wars lie inside the life); the civil war itself ran to the 1845 unification (History of Tonga page).

certainty.note: Oral-tradition chronology throughout: the capitals' spans, the tributaries' years and the 1100 and 1250 dates are placings within the pages' centuries; only the island coasts are sharp.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks. Chronology is oral-tradition and the pages give centuries, not years: the 1100 incorporation of the Tongan group and the tributaries, the 1250 Samoan expulsion ('13th or 14th century'), the 1450/1600 ʻUvea-Futuna span and the 1535 lapse of the outer tributaries are placings at confidence 1 and are the reviewer's first targets. End year: this dossier ends the state at the 1799 murder of Tukuʻaho (History of Tonga) rather than at the 1865 abolition of the Tuʻi Tonga title (the empire page's infobox), because the title had no state after 1799; the Kingdom of Tonga (1845) is the successor across a 46-year interregnum drawn as nobody's land. Region names: the Manuʻa exclusion from Samoa uses a radius; gazetteer_names_needed: Manuʻa Islands, Lau Islands, Niuas; 'Wallis and Futuna Is.' is assumed to be the Natural Earth spelling (check). Capitals' coordinates are approximate. Nauru, Kiribati and Tuvalu are named in the realm's list but not drawn.
